$comment: NBA 2K27 BADGE TOKENS AND SLOTS.
SOURCED from 2K's official MyPLAYER Builder page:
- Every build starts with 20 Badge slots across six disciplines: Shooting, Finishing, Playmaking,
Defense, Rebounding, Physicals. All 20 are available immediately; you must earn TOKENS to fill them.
- Meeting a badge's attribute requirement puts it in your INVENTORY. Spending tokens equips it.
- Tokens are earned by PLAYING — the six discipline progression meters, Team Practice drills and
Gatorade workouts — NOT by how you allocate attributes at build creation.
- Tokens can be reassigned at any time, but tokens earned in-game stay locked to their discipline.
- Bonus Slots and Bonus Tokens from Build Specialization, Seasons and Crews are discipline-agnostic.
- Rebirth immediately unlocks a percentage of your default tokens.
- TOKEN COST VARIES BY BODY: 'you can see in real time how your selected size and position affect
which Badges you qualify for and how many tokens each Badge will cost. Taller players may see a
different number of tokens required than shorter ones for the same Badge.'
THIS CHANGES THE DEFAULT MODEL. An earlier version derived tokens from attribute investment. That is
wrong: tokens are a progression resource, so how many you have is a fact about YOUR ACCOUNT, not about
the build. The default is now a flat per-discipline pool you set to match your own progress, and the
UI exposes it. `linear-by-investment` is retained only as a fallback for planning in the abstract.
STILL NOT SOURCED: the size of the token pool at any progression level, the per-discipline slot split,
the height/position cost adjustment, and whether upgrading a tier pays the difference or the full price.

verification.notes: The mechanic, the 20 slots, the six disciplines, how tokens are earned and that cost varies by size/position are all official. Every QUANTITY below is not.

'absolute' = equipping Gold costs the full Gold price. 'incremental' = you pay Gold minus what you already paid for Silver. The charts show a per-tier price but not which of these it means. 'absolute' is the more conservative reading.

verification.source: 2K official: 'Every single build starts with 20 Badge slots distributed across six specific disciplines'.
verification.notes: The TOTAL of 20 is official. The per-discipline SPLIT below is invented — 2K does not publish it. Bonus Slots earned through Build Specialization, Seasons and Crews are not modelled.

$comment: mode 'flat' (default): use `flatByDiscipline`. Correct in KIND — tokens are earned by playing, so the
size of your pool is a property of your account, not of the build. Set it to what you actually have.
mode 'table': exact ratings that grant tokens. Retained in case 2K27 also grants some from attributes.
mode 'linear-by-investment': derive tokens from attribute spend. Known to be the WRONG model for 2K27;
kept only for planning an abstract 'fully progressed in what I invested in' build.
mode 'manual': treat as unlimited unless manualTokens says otherwise.

verification.source: 2K official for the mechanic; the numbers are invented.
verification.notes: flatByDiscipline is set so that badge SLOTS bind rather than tokens, matching '20 badge slots' being the headline constraint. Replace with your real counts.

progressionPresets.$comment: Rough multipliers on flatByDiscipline for the UI. Tokens are earned over time, so a fresh build has far fewer than a maxed account.

manualTokens.$comment: Set any of these to a number to override the computed token pool for that discipline. null = compute it. The UI exposes these as inputs so you can type your real in-game values.

verification.notes: 'You can reassign Tokens at any time, but Tokens earned through in-game events remain locked to their respective discipline.' Cap breakers not granting tokens is from 2K27 builder coverage.

$comment: What to charge for a badge tier whose real token cost is unknown.
WHY THIS EXISTS: the Rebounding and Physicals badge cost charts were never supplied, so 11 of the
53 badges have no sourced token cost. Without a fallback those badges can never be equipped, which
silently cripples every big-man and athleticism build — a worse failure than an approximate price.
WHY THIS SHAPE: all 42 badges whose costs ARE known fall into exactly three ladders and nothing
else: 1/3/4/5 (15 badges), 2/4/5/6 (10 badges) and 3/5/6/7 (17 badges). The middle ladder is used
here. That is an inference from a very consistent pattern, NOT a sourced value, and every badge
priced this way is flagged `tokenCostInferred` and called out in the UI.
Set `enabled` to false to go back to refusing to price them, which is the strictly honest option.

verification.source: Inferred from the cost ladders of the 42 badges with sourced token costs.
verification.notes: Replace with real costs from the Rebounding and Physicals badge cost charts and this fallback stops being used.

$comment: 2K states outright that badge token cost depends on your size and position: a taller player may pay a
different number of tokens for the same badge. The token costs in badges.json were read off charts
that do not say which body they were captured at, so they are a SINGLE-BODY SNAPSHOT.
`perInchHeight` adjusts a badge tier's cost by that many tokens per inch away from `referenceHeight`,
rounded and clamped to >= 1. It is 0 by default, i.e. 'no adjustment known' — NOT 'no adjustment
exists'. Set it once the direction and size are known, or fill `overrides` with exact costs.

verification.source: 2K official confirms cost VARIES by size and position; the magnitude and direction are not published.
verification.notes: perInchHeight is 0 so the app currently uses the chart costs unchanged. This is a known gap, surfaced in the UI.
